docs.title: Smart Expense Tracker
docs.text:
A personal expense management application

Smart Expense Tracker is a web-based application developed to help users record, organize and review their daily expenses. It provides an expense dashboard with category-wise spending visualization, expense search and Excel export functionality.

This documentation portal provides product information, user instructions, installation procedures, API references and troubleshooting guidance for the application.

docs.title: About the Project
docs.text:
Smart Expense Tracker consists of a React frontend, a Java Spring Boot backend and a PostgreSQL database.

The application communicates with the backend through REST APIs. JSON Web Tokens (JWT) are used in the authentication implementation.

The documentation describes the current implementation and identifies areas that require further validation or improvement.

docs.title: What You Can Do
docs.text: Feature Description User registration Create a user account. User login Log in using registered credentials. Add expenses Record an expense with its title, amount, category and date. Search expenses Find expenses using their title. Spending summary View the total spending displayed on the dashboard. Category visualization Review expense distribution using a pie chart. Excel export Export expense records for offline analysis. Delete expenses Delete individual expenses or clear the expense list.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Smart Expense Tracker is a web application that helps users record and review their personal expenses. Users can add expense details, view their spending information, search their expense records and export expense data for further analysis.

This documentation describes the application's current functionality, user workflows, technical architecture and known limitations.

docs.title: Intended Users
docs.text:
The application is intended for individuals who want to:

  • Record their day-to-day expenses.
  • Organize expenses using categories.
  • Review their spending history.
  • Understand spending distribution across categories.
  • Export expense records for offline analysis.

docs.title: User Registration and Login
docs.text: Users can register an account and log in using their email address and password.

docs.title: Expense Management
docs.text:
Users can add expenses by providing:

  • Expense title
  • Amount
  • Category
  • Date

The dashboard displays the available expense records and provides options to delete an individual expense or clear the expense list.

docs.title: Expense Search
docs.text: Users can search their expense records using the expense title.

docs.title: Spending Summary
docs.text: The dashboard displays the total spending calculated from the available expense records.

docs.title: Category-wise Visualization
docs.text: A pie chart displays the distribution of expenses across categories.

docs.title: Excel Export
docs.text: Users can export their expense records to an Excel file for offline review.

docs.title: Application Architecture
docs.text: The application consists of two primary components.

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text: The frontend is built using React. It provides the user interface for registration, login and expense management.

docs.title: Backend
docs.text: The backend is built using Java and Spring Boot. It exposes REST API endpoints and uses Spring Data JPA for database operations.

docs.title: Database
docs.text: The application is configured to use PostgreSQL for persistent storage.

docs.title: Technology Stack
docs.text: Component Technology Frontend React Backend Java, Spring Boot Data access Spring Data JPA, Hibernate Database PostgreSQL Authentication JSON Web Tokens (JWT) API communication REST, Axios Charts Chart.js Export Excel file export

docs.title: Current Scope and Limitations
docs.text:
The following points are important when interpreting the current implementation:

  • Expense editing is not currently available through the dashboard interface.
  • Some backend endpoints are not exposed through the current dashboard workflows.
  • Authentication and authorization controls require further security review.
  • The application should not be considered production-ready until the identified security issues are addressed.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
This document lists the REST API endpoints currently implemented in the Smart Expense Tracker backend.

The API is built using Java and Spring Boot. It provides endpoints for user registration, authentication, and expense management.

Base URL (local development):

http://localhost:8080

All endpoint paths listed below are relative to this base URL.

docs.title: 2. Authentication APIs
docs.text: Method Endpoint Description Request body POST /api/auth/register Registers a new user User details POST /api/auth/login Authenticates a user and returns a JWT Login credentials

docs.title: 2.1 Register a user
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/auth/register

Request body:

{
  "name": "Alex",
  "email": "alex@example.com",
  "password": "example-password"
}

Behaviour: - Checks whether the email address already exists. - Returns a bad-request response if the email is already registered. - Otherwise, saves the user and returns the saved user object.

Documentation and security note: The current implementation accepts and stores the password as plain text. The returned user object may also contain the password. Do not use real credentials when testing this endpoint.

docs.title: 2.2 Login
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/auth/login

Request body:

{
  "email": "alex@example.com",
  "password": "example-password"
}

Behaviour: - Looks up the user by email. - Returns 404 if the user is not found. - Returns 401 if the password does not match. - Returns a JWT token if authentication succeeds.

The current implementation returns the token as a plain response value.

docs.title: 3. Expense APIs
docs.text: Method Endpoint Description Authorization header in controller GET /api/expenses Retrieves expenses for the authenticated user Required POST /api/expenses Creates an expense for the authenticated user Required DELETE /api/expenses/all Deletes all expenses for the authenticated user Required DELETE /api/expenses/{id} Deletes an expense by ID Not checked PUT /api/expenses/{id} Updates an expense by ID Not checked GET /api/expenses/category/{category} Retrieves expenses by category Not checked GET /api/expenses/monthly?year={year}&month={month} Retrieves the monthly expense total Not checked GET /api/expenses/user/{userId} Retrieves expenses for a user ID Not checked DELETE /api/expenses/user/{userId} Deletes expenses for a user ID Not checked

docs.title: 3.1 Retrieve expenses
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/expenses

Request header:

Authorization: Bearer <JWT_TOKEN>

Behaviour: - Extracts the email address from the JWT. - Finds the corresponding user. - Returns the expenses associated with that user.

docs.title: 3.2 Create an expense
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/expenses

Request header:

Authorization: Bearer <JWT_TOKEN>

Request body:

{
  "title": "Groceries",
  "amount": 850.50,
  "category": "Food",
  "date": "2026-11-10"
}

Behaviour: - Extracts the user's email from the JWT. - Finds the corresponding user. - Associates the new expense with that user. - Saves and returns the expense.

docs.title: 3.3 Delete all expenses
docs.text:
Endpoint: DELETE /api/expenses/all

Request header:

Authorization: Bearer <JWT_TOKEN>

Behaviour: - Identifies the user from the JWT. - Deletes all expenses associated with that user.

docs.title: 3.4 Delete an expense by ID
docs.text:
Endpoint: DELETE /api/expenses/{id}

Path parameter: - id: ID of the expense to delete.

Behaviour: Deletes the expense with the supplied ID.

docs.title: 3.5 Update an expense
docs.text:
Endpoint: PUT /api/expenses/{id}

Path parameter: - id: ID of the expense to update.

Request body: Expense fields.

Behaviour: Passes the supplied ID and expense object to the expense service for updating.

docs.title: 3.6 Retrieve expenses by category
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/expenses/category/{category}

Path parameter: - category: Expense category to retrieve.

Behaviour: Returns expenses matching the supplied category.

docs.title: 3.7 Retrieve monthly expense total
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/expenses/monthly

Query parameters: - year: Year to retrieve. - month: Month number to retrieve.

Example:

GET /api/expenses/monthly?year=2026&month=11

Behaviour: Returns the calculated expense total for the supplied year and month.

docs.title: 3.8 Retrieve expenses by user ID
docs.text:
Endpoint: GET /api/expenses/user/{userId}

Path parameter: - userId: ID of the user.

Behaviour: Returns expenses associated with the supplied user ID.

docs.title: 3.9 Delete expenses by user ID
docs.text:
Endpoint: DELETE /api/expenses/user/{userId}

Path parameter: - userId: ID of the user.

Behaviour: Deletes expenses associated with the supplied user ID.

docs.title: 4. Important implementation limitations
docs.text:
The following observations were identified during source-code review:

  1. Passwords are currently stored and compared as plain text.
  2. The registration endpoint returns the saved user entity, which includes the password field.
  3. Several expense endpoints do not perform authentication or verify that the requested expense belongs to the requesting user.
  4. The JWT secret is hard-coded in the current implementation.
  5. Some backend endpoints are not exposed through the current frontend dashboard.

These limitations must be addressed before the API is considered suitable for production use.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
This document describes error conditions identified in the Smart Expense Tracker API.

It provides developers with information about authentication failures, invalid requests, and troubleshooting considerations.

The HTTP status codes below are based on the current controller implementation where specified. Other responses must be verified through local API testing.

docs.title: 2.1 Duplicate email during registration
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/auth/register

HTTP status: 400 Bad Request

Cause:

The supplied email address is already registered.

Recommended action:

Use a different email address or sign in using the existing account.

docs.title: 2.2 Incorrect password
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/auth/login

HTTP status: 401 Unauthorized

Cause:

The supplied password does not match the stored password.

Recommended action:

Check the supplied credentials and try again.

docs.title: 2.3 User account not found
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/auth/login

HTTP status: 404 Not Found

Cause:

No account was found for the supplied email address.

Recommended action:

Check the email address or register a new account.

docs.title: 3.1 Missing authorization token
docs.text:
Affected endpoint: GET /api/expenses

Cause:

The request does not include the required Authorization header.

Recommended action:

Include a valid JWT in the request header:

Authorization: Bearer <JWT_TOKEN>

The exact HTTP response for a missing token must be verified against the running application.

docs.title: 3.2 Invalid or expired token
docs.text:
Affected endpoint: GET /api/expenses

Cause:

The supplied token may be malformed, invalid, or expired.

Recommended action:

Sign in again and use a newly generated token.

The actual HTTP status and response body must be verified through testing.

docs.title: 4. General Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Possible cause Recommended investigation Cannot connect to API Backend is not running Check the Spring Boot application Connection refused Incorrect port or server address Verify the configured server port Database connection failure Database configuration issue Check database URL and credentials Unexpected response Request format or backend behaviour Inspect the Postman request and response Expense list is empty No matching expense records Verify the test account and database records

docs.title: 5. Security Considerations
docs.text:
The current implementation has known security limitations:

  • Passwords are stored and compared as plain text.
  • The JWT signing secret is hard-coded.
  • Some expense endpoints do not enforce authentication.
  • Some operations do not verify expense ownership.

Do not expose real credentials, JWT tokens, or personal financial data in error reports or documentation examples.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
The Smart Expense Tracker REST API provides backend services for user authentication and expense management.

The API is developed using Java and Spring Boot. It communicates with the frontend application through HTTP requests and returns data in JSON format where applicable.

This documentation is intended for developers who want to understand, test, or integrate with the application's backend services.

docs.title: 2. API Base URL
docs.text:
For local development, the backend API runs on:

http://localhost:8080

API endpoints are accessed by appending their paths to this base URL.

For example:

http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login

The port may differ depending on the backend configuration.

docs.title: 3. Technology
docs.text:
The backend uses the following technologies:

Technology Purpose Java Backend programming language Spring Boot Application framework Spring Data JPA Database access Hibernate Object-relational mapping PostgreSQL Relational database JSON Data exchange format JWT Token generation and authentication

docs.title: 4. API Categories
docs.text: The available endpoints are grouped into two main categories.

docs.title: Authentication APIs
docs.text:
These endpoints support user registration and login.

  • Register a new user.
  • Authenticate an existing user.
  • Generate a JSON Web Token (JWT) after successful login.

docs.title: Expense APIs
docs.text:
These endpoints support expense-related operations.

  • Retrieve expenses.
  • Create an expense.
  • Update an expense.
  • Delete an expense.
  • Retrieve expenses by category.
  • Calculate monthly expense totals.
  • Retrieve or delete expenses associated with a user ID.

Refer to the API Endpoint Inventory for the complete endpoint list.

docs.title: 5. Authentication
docs.text:
The application uses JSON Web Tokens (JWT) for certain expense API operations.

For endpoints that require authentication, include the token in the HTTP request header:

Authorization: Bearer <JWT_TOKEN>

To obtain a token, first send a login request using the authentication API.

Important: Authentication is not consistently enforced across all currently implemented expense endpoints. Some endpoints do not verify the requesting user's identity or ownership of the requested data. Review the endpoint inventory and the application's security limitations before using these APIs.

docs.title: 6. Request and Response Format
docs.text:
The API uses HTTP methods to perform operations:

HTTP method General purpose GET Retrieve information POST Submit information or create a resource PUT Update a resource DELETE Remove a resource

JSON is used for request and response data where applicable.

The exact request fields and response formats depend on the individual endpoint.

docs.title: 7. Error Handling
docs.text:
The current implementation uses HTTP status codes for some authentication outcomes, including:

Status code Meaning in the current authentication implementation 401 Login password does not match 404 User account was not found 400 Registration email already exists

Other endpoint responses should be verified through local API testing before publishing detailed response examples.

docs.title: 8. Security Considerations
docs.text:
The current application is a learning and portfolio project. It should not be treated as production-ready.

The source-code review identified the following limitations:

  • Passwords are stored and compared as plain text.
  • The JWT signing secret is hard-coded.
  • The registration response may expose the password field.
  • Several expense endpoints do not enforce authentication and ownership checks.

Use fictional test data and a local development environment when testing. Do not use real passwords, financial information, or production credentials.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
This guide explains how to set up and run Smart Expense Tracker in a local development environment.

The application consists of a React frontend, a Java Spring Boot backend and a PostgreSQL database.

Follow the instructions in sequence to prepare the development environment, configure the application and verify the installation.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Install the following software before proceeding.

Software Requirement Purpose Java Development Kit JDK 21 Runs the Spring Boot backend Apache Maven Version compatible with the project Builds and runs the backend Node.js Version compatible with the project dependencies Runs the React frontend npm Installed with Node.js Installs frontend dependencies PostgreSQL Supported PostgreSQL installation Stores application data Git Current stable version Clones the project repository Visual Studio Code or IntelliJ IDEA Optional Source code editing

Note: Confirm the exact Maven, Node.js and PostgreSQL versions used during your successful local setup before publishing this guide as a verified compatibility list.

docs.title: Step 1: Clone the Repository
docs.text:
Clone the Smart Expense Tracker repository to your local machine.

Open a terminal and execute:

git clone https://github.com/YogeshRoyal2003/Smart-Expense-Tracker.git

Navigate to the cloned project directory:

cd Smart-Expense-Tracker

The project contains separate directories for the backend and frontend.

Smart-Expense-Tracker/
├── Backend/
├── frontend/
└── README.md

docs.title: Step 2: Configure the PostgreSQL Database
docs.text:
Ensure that PostgreSQL is installed and running.

Create a database for the application using your PostgreSQL client.

For example:

CREATE DATABASE smart_expense_tracker;

Record the database connection details. These will be used when configuring the backend.

The database URL generally follows this format:

jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/smart_expense_tracker

Replace the database name, host and port if your local configuration is different.

docs.title: Step 3: Configure the Backend
docs.text:
Navigate to the backend directory:

cd Backend

The backend uses environment variables for database configuration.

Configure the following variables in your local environment:

Variable Description DATABASE_URL PostgreSQL JDBC connection URL DATABASE_USERNAME PostgreSQL database username DATABASE_PASSWORD PostgreSQL database password PORT Backend server port; defaults to 8080

Example PowerShell configuration:

$env:DATABASE_URL="jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/smart_expense_tracker"
$env:DATABASE_USERNAME="your_database_username"
$env:DATABASE_PASSWORD="your_database_password"
$env:PORT="8080"

Replace the example username and password with your local database credentials.

Do not commit passwords, JWT secrets or other sensitive configuration values to Git.

docs.title: Step 4: Build and Run the Backend
docs.text:
From the Backend directory, execute:

mvn clean install

After the build completes, start the Spring Boot application:

mvn spring-boot:run

The backend is configured to use port 8080 by default, unless another port is supplied through the PORT environment variable.

Check the terminal output for the Spring Boot startup messages.

docs.title: Step 5: Configure the Frontend
docs.text:
Open a separate terminal.

Navigate to the frontend directory:

cd frontend

Install the required dependencies:

npm install

Inspect the frontend API configuration in:

src/services/api.js

Ensure that the frontend is configured to communicate with your locally running backend when performing a local development setup.

The backend API uses the /api path. Confirm the correct local API base URL before starting the frontend.

docs.title: Step 6: Start the Frontend
docs.text:
Check the scripts section in frontend/package.json to identify the configured development command.

If the project defines the usual React start script, execute:

npm start

Otherwise, use the command specified by the project.

Wait for the frontend development server to start and open the local address displayed in the terminal.

docs.title: Step 7: Verify the Installation
docs.text:
Perform the following checks:

  1. Confirm that the frontend application loads in the browser.
  2. Open the registration page.
  3. Register a test account using non-sensitive test data.
  4. Log in with the registered account.
  5. Add an expense with a title, amount, category and date.
  6. Confirm that the expense appears in the dashboard.
  7. Refresh the dashboard and check whether the expense remains available.
  8. Verify that the total spending and category chart reflect the recorded expense.
  9. Test the Excel export functionality.

If these operations work as expected, the local application setup has passed the basic functional verification.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
The Smart Expense Tracker dashboard provides users with an interface to record, search and review their personal expenses.

Users can add expense records, view their spending summary, analyze expenses by category, search existing records and export expense information to an Excel file.

This guide explains how to use the available dashboard features.

docs.title: Accessing the Dashboard
docs.text:
Figure 1: Smart Expense Tracker dashboard.

  1. Open Smart Expense Tracker in your browser.
  2. Navigate to the login page.
  3. Enter your registered email address and password.
  4. Submit the login form.
  5. After successful authentication, access the dashboard.

Note: The dashboard requires a registered user account.

docs.title: Understanding the Dashboard
docs.text:
The dashboard provides access to the application's expense management functionality.

The main capabilities include:

  • Adding new expenses.
  • Viewing expense records.
  • Searching expenses by title.
  • Reviewing total spending.
  • Viewing category-wise spending distribution.
  • Exporting expense records.
  • Deleting expense records.

docs.title: Adding an Expense
docs.text:
Figure 2: Add Expense to the List.

Use the expense form to record a new expense.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Open the dashboard.
  2. Locate the expense entry form.
  3. Enter the expense title.
  4. Enter the expense amount.
  5. Select or enter the expense category as supported by the interface.
  6. Select the expense date.
  7. Submit the form.

docs.title: Expected Result
docs.text: The application submits the expense information to the backend. When the operation succeeds, the expense should appear in the dashboard's expense records.

docs.title: Viewing Expense Records
docs.text:
The dashboard displays the expense records available to the logged-in user.

Review the displayed information to identify the recorded expenses.

The information associated with an expense includes:

  • Expense title.
  • Amount.
  • Category.
  • Date.

docs.title: Searching for an Expense
docs.text:
Use the search functionality to find an expense by its title.

Figure 3: Smart Expense Tracker Expense Search.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Locate the search field on the dashboard.
  2. Enter the title or a matching portion of the title.
  3. Review the filtered expense records.

docs.title: Expected Result
docs.text:
The dashboard displays the expense records matching the entered search text.

Note: The current implementation performs title-based searching in the frontend.

docs.title: Reviewing Total Spending
docs.text:
The dashboard displays a total spending value calculated from the available expense records.

Use this summary to review the total amount represented by the displayed expense data.

docs.title: Understanding the Category Chart
docs.text:
Figure 4: Category Chart.

The dashboard includes a pie chart that visualizes expense distribution across categories.

The chart helps users understand how their recorded expenses are distributed among different categories.

Review the category segments to identify the relative contribution of each category to the recorded expenses.

docs.title: Exporting Expense Records
docs.text:
Figure 5: Exporting Data to Excel.

Users can download their expense records as an Excel file.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Open the dashboard.
  2. Locate the Excel export option.
  3. Select the export option.
  4. Check the downloaded file.
  5. Open the file using a compatible spreadsheet application.

docs.title: Expected Result
docs.text: An Excel file containing the exported expense information is downloaded to the user's device.

docs.title: Deleting an Individual Expense
docs.text: Users can remove an individual expense record from the dashboard.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Locate the expense record.
  2. Select its delete option.
  3. Complete any confirmation step presented by the application, if applicable.
  4. Check the updated expense list.

docs.title: Expected Result
docs.text: The selected expense is removed if the delete operation succeeds.

docs.title: Deleting All Expenses
docs.text:
The dashboard also provides an option to delete all expense records.

Warning: This operation may permanently remove the user's expense records. Review the records carefully before proceeding.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Locate the delete-all option.
  2. Review the action before selecting it.
  3. Complete any confirmation step presented by the application, if applicable.
  4. Check the updated dashboard.

docs.title: Expected Result
docs.text: The expense list is cleared if the delete operation succeeds.
